Priya to share Dedicated pricing sheet and 12-month commit options
Jordan to provide onboarding checklist and contract intake form

summary: Kickoff between Redwood and BlueWave Financial procurement/legal to start vendor onboarding. Reviewed outstanding MSA/DPA items, SLAs, pricing approval path, and security artifacts. Agreed on redline exchange and technical deep-dive to validate Dedicated deployment and KMS/retention controls.

Security artifacts: SOC2, ISO, KMS, VPC/networking
transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-11-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Samantha (BlueWave Procurement), Derek (BlueWave Legal), Maya (BlueWave Security), Roberto (Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick intake to capture legal exceptions and procurement path; agree next steps for redlines and technical deep-dive.

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can folks introduce themselves real quick? Sorry if there's any audio lag.
[00:16] Samantha: Hi, Sam Ortiz, Head of Procurement at BlueWave. I'll own the vendor intake process.
[00:22] Derek: Derek Huang, legal counsel — I'll be reviewing the MSA and DPA.
[00:26] Maya: Maya Singh, Cloud Security. I'll check the SOC, encryption, KMS and network requirements.
[00:31] Roberto: Roberto Alvarez, VP Eng, I'll be partnering with Maya on the technical test and pilot.
[00:36] Ethan: Great, Ethan Patel from Redwood AE, and Priya our SE, Jordan CSM — thanks.
[00:42] Priya: Hi all. Quick note — we'll focus on clarifying the MSA/DPA gaps, SLA targets you need, and get you a committed pricing option for Dedicated capacity.

[01:05] Samantha: To frame this, procurement timeline is tight — we have a vendor committee on 12/10 and procurement sign-off prefer by 12/16. We'll need legal redlines before that so pricing and risk can go to the committee.
[01:20] Derek: Yep — the main DPA ask is around data residency and subprocessor disclosures. Also we'll need to confirm retention windows and deletion guarantees.
[01:33] Maya: On security side, SOC2 attestation is necessary, ideally the ISO cert too. We also need KMS integration options if we go private — customer-managed keys, HSM or KMS, and audit logs for key use.

[02:05] Priya: Understood. For Redwood Private we support customer KMS pairings, and our Dedicated offer can be deployed into a customer VPC for network isolation. There are a couple of patterns: customer-managed encryption keys via HSM/KMS or platform-managed with strong envelope encryption. I'll send a short doc with tradeoffs.
[02:35] Roberto: If we do VPC, what level of access do you require? We want to avoid broad inbound rules.
[02:41] Priya: Typically just a small set of egress/peering rules and an ingress load balancer. We can do private peering or tech-proxy; I'll inventory the exact ports/ips.

[03:10] Ethan: On the MSA, there are usually three categories you see objections on: liability caps, data handling/liability around training, and termination/transition. Derek, anything specific you want us to flag?
[03:24] Derek: Liability cap is standard — but we have an ask to include carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct. Also, we want explicit language that customer data will never be used to train any public models.
[03:39] Ethan: We can commit to non-training of customer data for shared models, we have language in our DPA — but we'll send a redline that makes that explicit.
[03:48] Priya: One small caveat — for Hosted API we have telemetry and aggregate metrics. For Private or Dedicated we can lock that down.

[04:12] Samantha: Pricing is a committee concern. Can you outline committed capacity discounts vs on-demand? We need a 12-month price table to compare.
[04:24] Priya: Yes. We have a pricing sheet: on-demand, reserved/dedicated, and enterprise committed SKU. I'll produce three scenarios: 6-month pilot (burst), 12-month reserved commit (discounted), and a 12-month enterprise with SLA.
[04:40] Ethan: We'll also include a TCO note showing token-cost delta and expected throughput for your workload.

[05:05] Maya: On retention — what's the default? We need logs retained for 12 months for audits, but customer payload retention should be configurable; ideally a 30-day default with options.
[05:17] Priya: Default for hosted is 30 days; for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention to meet your policy and add audit retention for logs to 12 months.

[05:45] Derek: On subprocessors — can you provide a list and attestations? We need to know where data flows, esp. cloud vendors.
[05:52] Ethan: Yes, we'll share our subprocessor list and we can mark the EU/US boundaries. We'll also attach SOC2 and ISO or equivalent artifacts.

[06:22] Samantha: For procurement, we need the procurement intake form filled — legal wants to see the redlines + SOC2 + pricing + the onboarding checklist.
[06:31] Jordan: I'll send the Redwood onboarding checklist and the intake form by EOD today.

[06:52] Priya: Quick question to Roberto — can you outline the pilot success criteria? Latency targets, throughput, and what endpoints you plan to call?
[07:03] Roberto: We want 95th percentile latency under 250ms for short prompts and a throughput of about 200 reqs/sec initially. Also want embedding throughput for search indexing — approx 80 qps.
[07:18] Priya: Okay, that helps. We'll map those to expected GPU configs and provide perf numbers. We may suggest a different model quant or batching to hit those latencies at cost targets.

[08:00] Derek: Back to contract — do you have standard SLA language and outage credits? Our security team wants clear MTTR commitments and credits if SLA is missed.
[08:10] Ethan: Yes, we have SLA SLOs for uptime and latency tiers and a credit table for breaches. For Dedicated customers we can negotiate stricter SLOs and higher credits. We'll include our standard SLA + a Dedicated SLA appendix.

[09:00] Maya: Also need to confirm logging — do you provide audit logs of user actions and key usage? For compliance we'll need immutable logs with tamper evidence.
[09:12] Priya: We produce audit logs with timestamps, and for Private deployments we can route logs to your SIEM. Tamper-evidence is supported via append-only storage and signed log shipping. I'll add the details.

[10:05] Samantha: The committee will ask about vendor risk registry and incident response. Do you have an IR playbook and incident SLA?
[10:16] Jordan: Yes, we have a vendor incident response playbook and an on-call escalation matrix. We can share a redacted playbook and define the IR RTO/RPO expectations.

[11:00] Ethan: Let's talk schedule: Sam, you said committee on 12/10 and procurement sign-off 12/16. To make that we need redlines back to you by end of week of 12/1 at the latest. Is that feasible?
[11:12] Samantha: Yes, if legal can provide exceptions this week, then procurement can prep the packet. Derek, can you review and send any absolute no-go items by Monday?
[11:22] Derek: I'll aim to return a prioritized list by Monday 12/1. I can't promise everything but I'll mark critical exceptions.

[12:00] Priya: For pricing approval, who signs off internally at BlueWave? Is it procurement or finance?
[12:08] Samantha: Procurement + Finance need to both sign; VP Eng Roberto will weigh in on technical fit. Final approval requires Procurement and Finance.

[12:26] Roberto: Also, for the pilot we may need to run a short performance benchmark in our staging — can Redwood provide a perf harness or a small test account?
[12:35] Priya: Yes, we can provide a perf harness and sample load script. For Dedicated pilots we can stand up a sandbox Dedicated cluster for 2–4 weeks.

[13:05] Ethan: I'm noting three primary decision items: legal redlines (MSA/DPA), pricing/commit level, and security deep-dive for Dedicated.
[13:17] Maya: One more: encryption key rotation and access — we need to confirm who holds key custody and the process when keys are rotated or revoked.
[13:27] Priya: We'll include a KMS integration appendix. For customer-managed keys, you control rotation; for platform-managed we rotate with audit events and you can request exports of rotation logs.

[14:00] Samantha: Any competitors or pricing comparisons we should be aware of? We're looking at CloudAI and VendorX — pricing is a big differentiator.
[14:09] Ethan: Understood. We'll include a short TCO that compares on-demand vs reserved and highlight where Redwood Dedicated reduces cost for steady throughput.

[15:00] Derek: About the DPA — can you strike or add explicit language around retention and demonstrable deletion, and certification that backups containing customer data are also purged on deletion requests?
[15:13] Ethan: We'll propose a clause that defines deletion to include primary stores and backups within a reasonable window and provide attestations. We'll also propose a 30-90 day backup purge period depending on configuration — we'll put options.

[16:00] Priya: For the technical deep-dive, who should attend from BlueWave? Priya: SEs and infra leads ideally.
[16:08] Roberto: Myself and one infra engineer, maybe Maya as well.

[17:00] Jordan: I'll circulate the onboarding intake and link to our contract intake template. Also I'll capture the committee dates.

[18:00] Ethan: Recap of next steps — we will send: redlined MSA + DPA, SOC2/ISO and subprocessor list, Dedicated pricing scenarios, onboarding checklist, and propose times for technical deep-dive.
[18:18] Samantha: Sounds good. We prefer the redlines by 12/2 so legal can do an internal pre-review.
[18:26] Derek: I'll aim to have initial exceptions by 12/1.

[19:00] Priya: I'll pack the Dedicated perf numbers and a sample config for the 200rps/250ms target and the embedding throughput.

[20:00] Ethan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep-dive. Appreciate the time.

Links shared: Redwood onboarding checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding-checklist), SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2-summary), Dedicated pricing template (link: https://redwood.example.com/dedicated-pricing).
notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (kms/K M S, Redwood Privatee). Customer timeline is tight — committee 12/10. Prioritize MSA/DPA redlines.
